name: First Fort Dearborn — the Indian agent's house

documented_range.note: THE RANGE IS INFERRED, NOT DATED FOR THIS BUILDING. It opens on 25 January 1808, the date Whistler's draught carries, which is the one day on which a source shows it standing. It may well be older: the factory and the agency were set up at the post in the years after 1803, and nothing in the corpus dates either house. It closes on 16 August 1812 with the first fort, the day after the evacuation, when the post was burned (data/exclusions.json fort_dearborn_first_1803). No source in the corpus says these houses burned with it. Closing them with the fort is the conservative reading: it keeps them out of every later scene and adds nothing to one.

placement.position_note: PLACED BY T-2062's RULE, NOT MEASURED. The draught lays down the garrison at twenty feet to the inch and says the buildings outside it are 'not laid down by a scale', so this box is the sheet's ARRANGEMENT opened out about the main gate. The sheet box is px [553, 1255, 629, 1356]. Its offset from the gate's mouth (px [964, 1150]) is multiplied by 3.322, the ratio of the drafter's 'Distance to Main Gate Eighteen Perches' (297 ft) to the 89 ft the sheet draws for the agent's house. The rule and its numbers are data/traces/whistler_1808_fort_dearborn.json § outside_the_stockade, and tools/read_whistler_1808.py --check (run by check.sh) refuses this point if it is not what the rule gives, to 0.01 m. Seated with the fort's own frame: the staff's foot at local E +1152, N +221, the frame's north on grid north. The rule is a reconstruction (docs/LIBERTIES.md), so this position carries the drafter's own disagreement between his figures: his two stated distances open the sheet out 3.3 and 6.8 times.
placement.symbolic_location: Outside the first Fort Dearborn, in the frame of Whistler's 1808 draught (T-2062 rule, part 'agents_house'): E -298.9..-265.3 ft, N -193.3..-148.6 ft of the flagstaff's foot, facing east; this record's origin is the box's corner the seat names for that facing.

footprint.note: THE DRAWN BOX AT THE INDIAN DEPARTMENT'S STATED SCALE, forty feet to the inch, from the sheet box in the register. The drawing is a small pictorial elevation, roof and front together, so the box is an upper bound on the plan and the plan itself is reconstructed. The width runs along the front, north-south.

stories.note: The draught draws it like the factory, with two rows of lights in its front. No source states its storeys.

wall_height_m.note: Unattested. Two storeys of hewn log, about fifteen feet to the eaves.

construction.note: Quaife: the factor's and the agent's 'two log houses'. The Chicago Magazine of March 1857 calls the factory 'two-story log' too (quoted on chicagology_prefire052). That page is cited here in prose only: its rights are unresolved, so it does not stand under a built value.

roof_type.note: The draught draws a pitched roof falling to the west.

roof_pitch_deg.note: Unattested; the draught's pictorial roof gives no pitch.

loft.note: Two full storeys, so no loft is modelled.

chimneys.note: The draught draws a stack at each end of the roof.

function.note: Index no. 17, 'Agents House', the Indian Department's agency at the post. Quaife: the factor's and the agent's 'two log houses' stood 'a short distance to the southwest' of the fort.

citations.citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 1. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1884.

Quaife, Milo Milton. Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835: A Study of the Evolution of the Northwestern Frontier, together with a History of Fort Dearborn. Chicago: University of Chicago Press, 1913.
what_it_supplies: the 1808 Whistler draught index for the FIRST fort, with its scale and its distances
Major Long's 1816 report on the second fort under construction
a scholarly negative: no dimension of the second fort's stockade
what_it_does_not_supply: any plan or dimension of the 1816 fort

citations.citation: Whistler, Captain John. "Fort Dearborn" [draught of the garrison and its vicinity], dated in the parade 'January 25th 1808', with its 'Index annexed to the Draught of Fort Dearborn &c.' signed at Fort Dearborn 20 February 1808. Original in the files of the War Department, Washington. Reproduced as the plate 'Fort Dearborn and Vicinity in 1808. From the original draft by Captain Whistler in the archives of the War Department at Washington', facing p. 164 of Quaife, Chicago and the Old Northwest, 1673-1835 (Chicago, 1913); the index is printed in full in note 413 on the same pages.
what_it_supplies: the first fort's garrison in plan at a stated scale: the double row of pickets, the two blockhouses at the north-west and south-east angles, the four barracks ranges, the magazine, two small houses, the main gate, the parade and the flagstaff
the drafter's index of 34 numbered features, and the note that two of them (the covered way and the gutters) are omitted from their places
the arrangement of the factor's and agent's establishments, stables, gardens and the houses across the river, by position only and not to scale
what_it_does_not_supply: any building height: the folded elevations disagree with each other
the fort's bearing to true north: no north arrow was found on the reproduction
the covered way to the river and the gutters, which the index itself says are omitted
anything about the second fort of 1816

research_note: THE AGENT'S HOUSE, the one building outside the stockade whose distance the drafter states: 'Distance to Main Gate Eighteen Perches'. That figure is the expansion that places this house, the factory and the stables (T-2062). Nobody is placed in it (L1).
